narrative.benchmark_md: Peer set of 5 institutions locked in research Phase 0 (DMA-RES-ACCU-MB-20260504-0001). This set spans the digital maturity spectrum — from sector-leading (Meridian) to sector-lagging (Servus) — and includes direct Manitoba competitive peers (Steinbach, Cambrian) and a Salesforce-technology-aligned benchmark (Conexus). All peer scores estimated from public evidence.
narrative.issue_register_md: Issues identified during research that directly constrain capability scores through the severity-to-maturity cap mechanism. All issues are sourced from public evidence. This section is enriched with assessment-layer scoring impact analysis beyond the research report.

per_pillar_md.P1: Pillar 1 is Access Credit Union's closest-to-peer pillar — but the gap between strategic intent ( level 2.10, level 2.31) and execution capability ( level 1.09, level 1.10) defines the central strategic paradox of this institution. CEO Wiebe holds an explicit digital mandate. The governance board is technically credentialed. Yet the innovation infrastructure required to execute that mandate does not exist.
per_pillar_md.P2: Pillar 2 is the most critical pillar in this assessment — both for scoring urgency and for Salesforce opportunity concentration. The weighted gap of −0.73 versus peer median is the largest of the four pillars. Three of four P2 categories score below peer median; Personalization scores level 1.00 — a complete zero for 208,000 member-owners. The branch consolidations that begin June 2026 will transfer physical member service volume to digital channels and the 4-site MSC, making every P2 gap an operational risk, not just a competitive positioning concern.
per_pillar_md.P3: Pillar 3 is Access Credit Union's closest-to-peer pillar — the only one where the institution meets or marginally exceeds the sector benchmark (+0.07). This aggregate hides a critical internal contrast: Compliance at level 2.71 is the highest-scoring category in the entire assessment, powered by 13 merger integrations completed without a single DGCM or FINTRAC enforcement action; while Automation at level 1.35 sits below even the modest peer floor, reflecting complete absence of process automation despite the institution managing four categories of legacy system debt. The P3 story for Zennify is therefore two-sided: compliance strength is the conversation opener; automation and fraud analytics are the investment opportunity.
per_pillar_md.P4: Pillar 4 represents Access Credit Union's most urgent platform investment gap. Three of four P4 categories score at or near level 1.00 — Data Governance and Analytics & AI are complete zeros (every capability level 1.00); Cybersecurity at level 1.37 reflects a coordinator-level security function managing enterprise-scale risk. Only Technology Architecture (level 2.02) reflects genuine modern-adjacent capability — AWS, Docker, microservices, DevOps, Dynatrace APM are all deployed and confirmed. The CIO mandate explicitly includes Business Intelligence and Data Analytics — yet these exist only as aspiration, not execution. The gap between CIO Froese's stated mandate and operational reality is 0.02 in versus level 1.00 in and. This is the 'integration-machine-without-data-depth' paradox identified in the assessment synthesis.
